_comment: Sanitized reference for the project-local hooks. The live file is
.claude/settings.local.json, which is gitignored because it carries absolute
paths. Replace <repo-path> when reproducing on another machine.
Updated 2026-08-17. On the admin notebook the live file held no hooks at all,
so the commit gate this reference describes was not in effect there; the state
on the other workstation was not checked. Because this file is gitignored,
each machine has to be verified on its own: jq '.hooks' on the live file, not
a reading of this one. The PreToolUse entry below now points at a script in
the repository rather than an inline one-liner, so it can be tested instead of
trusted.
The deny list added 2026-08-21 mirrors the one in ~/.claude/settings.json, set
2026-08-17. Publishing stays outside the session: every push, pull request and
release is issued by hand from a terminal outside the session. Deny beats allow
regardless of which file is more specific, so a project-level allow rule cannot
reopen it - which is why the contradictory wildcard that used to sit in the live
allow list was removed rather than left as decoration.
The Stop entry answers with systemMessage, which shows the reminder and lets
the session end. The earlier form, additionalContext on Stop, is documented as
'continue the conversation' and was measured to do exactly that on 2026-09-17:
every turn end re-invoked the model with the reminder, five times in a row
with no input, until the entry was removed.
The guard's timeout is 120 s against a measured 24 s worst case (validator
12 s plus ansible-lint 11.5 s). A PreToolUse hook that times out does not
block the call - the documentation says so - so the margin is the difference
between a gate and a delay.

hooks.command: printf '{"systemMessage": "Per CLAUDE.md: before this session ends, record what was learned in devops-til (new concepts as new .md files, README index updated), then push it."}'
